name: Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva
current_role: VP Engineering, GitKraken (per 2025/26 speaker bio); co-founder and former Chief Architect of Reltio
profile: Russian-born software architect who co-founded master-data-management company Reltio with CEO Manish Sood in 2011, serving as technical co-founder, Chief Architect and VP Platform Product Management. She has since held engineering leadership roles at Redpanda Data and is now VP Engineering at developer-tools company GitKraken.
interesting_fact: Won the 2018 Aragon Research Women in Technology Award (CIO category) as Reltio's Chief Architect.
deep_cut_fact: Before Reltio she designed core components of the Informatica MDM tool; she holds an MS in CS from Chelyabinsk State University (research in distributed graph computing), and Reltio's earliest brainstorms took place in Mountain View coffee shops.
notes: Appears to have left Reltio; current role at GitKraken per SF Engineering Leadership Community speaker page (https://sfelc.com/speaker/anastasia-zamyshlyaeva-2). Low public profile; no published contacts found. Best route likely via conference speaking circuits (LeadDev/SFELC).

name: Todd Crawford
current_role: Co-Founder and VP Strategic Initiatives, impact.com
profile: Affiliate-marketing pioneer who was on the founding team of Commission Junction (CJ) in 1998, later guided strategy for Digital River's OneNetworkDirect, and in 2008 co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com), the Santa Barbara partnership-automation platform. He remains VP of Strategic Initiatives and co-hosts the company's Partnership Economy podcast.
interesting_fact: Industry peers call him the 'Godfather of Affiliate'; he was named to PartnerCentric/Hello Partner's Hero100 2025 as 'The OG Hero'.
deep_cut_fact: He was an original board member of the Performance Marketing Association, the US affiliate-industry trade group, and has offered paid one-on-one advice calls on Clarity.fm.
notes: Very approachable, conference-circuit regular; his Clarity.fm paid-call profile is a direct route. Some sources describe him as CJ's first employee rather than co-founder.

name: Fahri Diner
current_role: Co-founder (and longtime CEO) of Plume Design; Executive Chairman of Aliro (quantum networking) since June 2026
profile: Telecom entrepreneur who founded optical-networking firm Qtera, sold to Nortel in 2000 for $3.25B, then became a VC (Applied Materials Ventures, Sigma Partners). He co-founded Plume in 2014-15, building a cloud SaaS platform for smart home Wi-Fi sold through broadband providers, and in 2026 became executive chairman of quantum-networking startup Aliro.
interesting_fact: His first startup, Qtera (ultra-long-haul photonic networking), was acquired by Nortel Networks for about $3.25 billion at the height of the optical boom.
deep_cut_fact: In November 2002, after Qtera, he joined Applied Materials Ventures in Menlo Park as a general partner investing in early-stage communications companies.
notes: Whether he is still Plume CEO in 2026 is unclear (one profile lists CEO 2014-2024). Crunchbase lists his self-styled title as 'Chief Servant of Plume's people, Customers & Stakeholders'. Aliro press office is another route.

name: Ed Felten
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Offchain Labs (developer of Arbitrum); Robert E. Kahn Professor of CS and Public Affairs emeritus, Princeton
profile: Princeton computer scientist and security researcher who was the FTC's first Chief Technologist (2011) and Deputy US CTO in the Obama White House (2015-17). In 2018 he co-founded Offchain Labs with former Princeton students Steven Goldfeder and Harry Kalodner; its Arbitrum rollup became the largest Ethereum layer-2. He served on the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board until January 2025 and still keynotes events like EthCC 2026.
interesting_fact: As the US government's witness in United States v. Microsoft, he demonstrated in court a tool built with two students that removed Internet Explorer access from Windows 98, rebutting Microsoft's claim that it couldn't be done.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a physicist: after a Caltech BS in physics (1985) he spent three years as a staff programmer on a Caltech parallel-supercomputer project before his CS PhD at the University of Washington, where his thesis was on communication protocols between parallel processors.

public_contacts.value: Freedom to Tinker (blog he founded/writes for): https://freedom-to-tinker.com

notes: Princeton email is from his (older) self-published faculty homepage, written as 'felten at cs dot princeton dot edu'; may be less monitored now. Frequent podcast guest and conference speaker, so a podcast invitation fits him well. Also a NAE member and former EFF board member.

name: Harry Franks
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Zego (stepped away from day-to-day role; Zego says he still provides 'ongoing support')
profile: London entrepreneur who co-founded Zego in 2016 with fellow Deliveroo alumnus Sten Saar after seeing how hard it was for couriers to get flexible insurance. Zego's pay-as-you-go and fleet insurance for gig-economy drivers made it a UK insurtech unicorn. Franks later left the company; no new venture has been publicly announced.
interesting_fact: Zego was born at Deliveroo: Franks saw first-hand that the company's couriers struggled to buy insurance that matched their part-time, on-demand work.
deep_cut_fact: He had no insurance background: before Zego he was Deliveroo's global head of procurement and earlier worked at luxury home-rental startup onefinestay.
notes: Left Zego (reported by Insurance Post / Insurance Times, citing personal reasons); keep outreach light. Low public profile since; no published personal contact found. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Tyler Kennedy
current_role: Co-founder and SVP Operations, Fetch (Madison, WI) - per UW-Madison 2023 materials
profile: UW-Madison business graduate (BBA '13) who co-founded Fetch Rewards with Wes Schroll; the receipt-scanning rewards app grew from a 2012 class business-plan assignment into a Madison-based company valued above $2B. He has led operations at Fetch and received UW-Madison's 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award.
interesting_fact: Fetch began as a business-plan assignment in a Wisconsin School of Business entrepreneurship class in 2012; Kennedy met Schroll via the campus Collegiate Entrepreneurs Organization.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fetch he mowed neighborhood lawns as a kid and later ran a boat-cleaning business in Milwaukee: 'I saw early on that the people who had the most time freedom were business owners.'
notes: Low-profile operator; CEO Wes Schroll is Fetch's public face. Current title not confirmed beyond 2023 UW sources. Name is common (not to be confused with others named Tyler Kennedy).

name: Roee Goldberg
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Atmospheric AI (London; raw-material supply-chain modeling)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who joined Spot.IM (now OpenWeb) as co-founder and COO in 2014, helping build the publisher comment/conversation platform into a unicorn before leaving the COO role around January 2022. In 2025 he founded London-based Atmospheric AI, which builds digital twins of raw-material supply chains (cost, resilience, emissions) and raised a $10M seed led by DBL Partners in November 2026.
interesting_fact: Atmospheric AI models tens of thousands of industrial plants 'between the well and your factory gate' so manufacturers can see the true cost and carbon of what they buy; the seed will extend models from plastics into chemicals, paper and metals.
deep_cut_fact: Before OpenWeb he was co-founder and CEO of a startup called Servito.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/climate podcast: just raised a seed for a climate/industrial supply-chain AI company (Axios exclusive, Nov 2026). Some sources say he advises Tech Nation's Climate Growth Programme (unverified). Wikipedia credits OpenWeb's founding to Nadav Shoval and Ishay Green only.

name: Henrique Fernandes
current_role: Historic co-founder (logistics) of Vestiaire Collective; current role unknown
profile: One of six co-founders of Paris-based luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective (founded 2009 as 'Vestiaire de Copines' with Fanny Moizant, Sophie Hersan, Sebastien Fabre, Alexandre Cognard and Christian Jorge), where he headed logistics. Very little public information exists on his later activities.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire Collective began life as 'Vestiaire de Copines' (a 'girlfriends' wardrobe'), later growing into a global pre-owned luxury platform backed by Kering.
notes: Extremely private; no personal web presence found. FrenchWeb lists him as 'cofondateur historique, logistique' (https://www.frenchweb.fr/henrique-fernandes). Name is common, so identity beyond the co-founder listing is uncertain. Route via Vestiaire Collective press office or LinkedIn.

name: Ronen Assia
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director, eToro (Nasdaq: ETOR); Managing Partner (Fintech), Team8
profile: Israeli designer-turned-entrepreneur who co-founded social-trading platform eToro in 2007 with his brother Yoni Assia and David Ring, serving as Chief Product Officer running product and engineering until 2020. He remains an eToro director after its May 2025 Nasdaq IPO and is a Managing Partner at Team8, building and investing in fintech startups.
interesting_fact: eToro pioneered 'social investing', letting users copy other traders' portfolios; it now serves over 30 million registered users in 100+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an industrial designer (BA Bezalel Academy, MA Product Design at London's Royal College of Art) and designed medical devices and household appliances before co-founding eToro.
notes: Brother Yoni Assia is eToro's CEO and public face. Ronen is reachable through Team8 (Tel Aviv VC/venture studio), which is the more natural route. Reportedly joined Riskified's board (per Riskified IR page).

name: Eimantas Sabaliauskas
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Tesonet; co-founder, Nord Security (NordVPN)
profile: Lithuanian entrepreneur who co-founded Vilnius venture builder Tesonet with Tomas Okmanas in 2008 and, with childhood friends, launched NordVPN in 2012-13, growing Nord Security into a $3B cybersecurity group (NordVPN, NordPass, NordLayer and more). Tesonet has also spawned or backed Hostinger, Oxylabs, Surfshark, CAST AI and nexos.ai and employs 4,200+ people across its group.
interesting_fact: Tesonet started for a single project and it took 34 different projects and ideas, from web hosting and e-commerce to video games, before NordVPN became its first global hit.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Tomas Okmanas first met in an IRC chat channel in 1999, nearly a decade before founding Tesonet together.
notes: Lower profile than co-founder Tomas Okmanas, who does most media. Tesonet also invests in sports (BC Zalgiris, London Lions). Search budget ran out before checking for personal social accounts.

name: Khairil Aizat
profile: Listed by Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2022-2024) as a founder of CoinTracker, the crypto portfolio and tax software company valued around $1B. CoinTracker's widely reported co-founders are Chandan Lodha and Jon Lerner; we could not verify any public link between Khairil Aizat and CoinTracker.
notes: Identity not confirmed: possible Hurun data error. Web search budget was exhausted before this could be checked further, and CoinTracker's site blocks automated fetches. Verify before any outreach.

name: Jan Wurzbacher
profile: German mechanical engineer who, with fellow ETH Zurich student Christoph Gebald, turned PhD research on capturing CO2 from ambient air into Climeworks, an ETH spin-off founded in 2009. Climeworks became the best-known direct air capture company, running its Orca and Mammoth plants in Iceland that store captured CO2 underground, and reached unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Climeworks' Mammoth plant in Iceland is among the largest direct-air-capture facilities in the world; the company now permanently stores captured CO2 underground rather than selling it.
deep_cut_fact: Climeworks' first commercial plant (Hinwil, 2017) sat on the roof of a waste incinerator using its waste heat, and its captured CO2 was sold to a nearby greenhouse as fertilizer and to Coca-Cola HBC to carbonate Valser sparkling water.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast (DAC is very energy-intensive; plants run on geothermal/renewables). Co-CEO Christoph Gebald often handles media. Climeworks site blocks automated fetching, so the press contact wasn't captured; check climeworks.com newsroom manually.

name: Tarun Chitra
current_role: Founder and CEO, Gauntlet (DeFi risk management and vault curation)
profile: Mathematician and quantitative researcher who founded Gauntlet (Gauntlet Networks) in 2018 to apply agent-based simulation and optimization to crypto protocols. Gauntlet became the leading risk manager for DeFi lending protocols and now also curates on-chain yield vaults for fintechs, exchanges and asset managers.
interesting_fact: He co-authored with Guillermo Angeris the 2020 paper 'Improved Price Oracles: Constant Function Market Makers', one of the foundational academic analyses of Uniswap-style automated market makers.
deep_cut_fact: As a Cornell math student his personal site hosted an essay on Bott periodicity, a separate music blog, and papers from Cornell's Mathematical Contest in Modeling, including a 2010 UAV-surveillance path-finding model.
notes: Deep-cut is from a c.2010 personal site under his name (Ithaca NY/Hockessin DE); it matches his known Cornell math background but was not cross-checked against a second source due to search limits. Very active on crypto podcasts and X; podcast invitation is a natural route.

name: Avi Perez
current_role: Chief Technology Officer and Co-Founder, Pyramid Analytics
profile: Co-founded business-intelligence software firm Pyramid Analytics in 2009 with Omri Kohl and Herbert Ochtman; he created and runs the Pyramid decision-intelligence platform, leading R&D and the technology roadmap. The Amsterdam/Tel Aviv-based company was backed early by Sequoia Capital (Series A, 2013) and reached unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Pyramid Analytics' Series A in 2013 was led by Sequoia Capital, and the company grew from a Microsoft-centric BI tool ('BI Office') into an AI-driven decision-intelligence platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before Pyramid he was co-founder and development manager of Urix, a US healthcare-informatics company, where he designed proprietary analytical systems; he holds a B.Com from UNSW in Australia and an MBA from Yale.
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via Pyramid's official bio. CEO Omri Kohl is the usual public spokesperson. No published press email found on Pyramid's newsroom.

name: Matt Creason
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of ShiftKey, the Dallas-based marketplace connecting nurses and other licensed healthcare professionals with open shifts (valued ~$2B). ShiftKey's own newsroom names Tom Ellis as founder & CEO and Ralph Marczynski as a co-founder; we could not find Matt Creason on ShiftKey's published pages.
notes: Identity/role at ShiftKey not verified (search budget exhausted). Contact listed is ShiftKey's company PR agency, not personal. Verify via LinkedIn before outreach.

name: Lu Cewu
current_role: Professor, School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Changjiang Distinguished Professor); co-founder of Flexiv (adaptive robotics)
profile: Chinese computer-vision and embodied-AI researcher who leads SJTU's Machine Vision and Intelligence Group (MVIG) and is listed by Hurun as a founder of Flexiv, the Shanghai/Silicon Valley maker of force-controlled adaptive robot arms valued around $1B. He trained at CUHK (PhD), HKUST and Stanford before joining SJTU.
interesting_fact: Named one of MIT Technology Review's 35 Innovators Under 35 (China) in 2018; in 2025 his group won the ICRA Best Paper Award on Human-Robot Interaction.
deep_cut_fact: Before returning to China he was a research fellow at Stanford working under Fei-Fei Li and Leonidas Guibas, after a PhD at CUHK supervised by Jiaya Jia.
notes: Email is his published SJTU lab address (lab page invites contact, mainly for recruiting). His Flexiv role (co-founder/chief scientist) comes from Hurun listing and was not confirmed on Flexiv's site in this pass. Mandarin outreach may land better.
